we have designed and synthesized a series of S-ribocysteinase inhibitors, and one of the inhibitors, a hemiaminal compound, showed time-dependent inhibition, which is consistent with enzyme-catalezed ring opening and formation of a more potent species.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel class of inhibitors that target bacterial interspecies communication.
the development of LuxS inhibitors as a new class of antibacterial agent.
the development of a series of novel LuxS inhibitors, which may provide a novel class for antibacterial agents and also serve as chemical probes for LuxS structure-function studies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the homocysteinyl thiol group and the 2'-hydroxyl group of the sugar moiety are the most critical for LuxS inhibition, while the endocyclic nitrogen atom of the sugar is not important for LuxS inhibition.

the LuxS active site is a very complex and dynamic structure and that a variety of compounds can be designed that can bind in different ways to this active site.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the [4-azasugar] moiety is not a good surrogate for the ribosyl moiety of SRH.
the LuxS active site is highly selective, but not rigid.
the LuxS active site is a unique and highly specific binding site for its natural substrate and the designed inhibitors.

LuxS inhibitors can be designed by using structural knowledge of the enzyme.
the LuxS active site is not as promiscuous as previously believed.
